findings.description: `deposit` now loads `DataKey::SupplyCap` with `.expect("supply cap missing")`. In Soroban, persistent entries can expire if TTL isn’t bumped; if `SupplyCap` expires, user deposits will trap rather than defaulting to `0` (cap disabled), creating a denial-of-service condition.
findings.recommendation: Either ensure `SupplyCap` is always TTL-bumped on all hot paths that call `deposit`/`seed_minimum_supply`, or restore a safe default (e.g., `unwrap_or(0u128)`) and treat missing as disabled cap.
findings.title: Resource Management: Persistent key expiry triggers panic in `deposit`

findings.description: `borrow_with_cash_policy` now reads `DataKey::BorrowCap` via `.expect("borrow cap missing")`. If `BorrowCap` expires from persistent storage (TTL not extended) or was never set in older deployments, borrows will trap, potentially freezing the market.
findings.recommendation: Ensure `BorrowCap` is included in persistent TTL extension on keeper/hot paths, or use `unwrap_or(0u128)` to fail open to `cap=0` (disabled) consistent with the initializer default.
findings.title: Resource Management: Persistent key expiry triggers panic in `borrow_with_cash_policy`

findings.description: `borrow_for_margin` now uses `.expect("borrow cap missing")` for `DataKey::BorrowCap`. If the `BorrowCap` persistent key expires, margin borrows will revert even when the intended default is `0` (cap disabled).
findings.recommendation: Bump TTL for `BorrowCap` alongside other core persistent keys, or revert to `unwrap_or(0u128)` for backward-compatible behavior under TTL expiry.
findings.title: Resource Management: Persistent key expiry triggers panic in `borrow_for_margin`
